author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the key to feeling more motivated and fulfilled lies in the tiny gaps between what we expect and what actually happens? By understanding how the brain uses prediction errors and dopamine to signal surprise, it becomes possible to design moments that lift energy, sharpen learning, and strengthen relationships. Small shifts—setting wiser goals, managing expectations, and creating well-timed delights—can effectively hack the brain’s reward system for a more satisfying life. 

Ashok Hegde is the William Harvey Professor of Biomedical Sciences at Georgia College where he runs a highly successful Pre-Med Mentoring Program, and teaches courses on neuroscience, physiology and histology, and mentors students in his lab engaging in research on synaptic plasticity. He did his dissertation research at the Center for Cellular and Molecular Biology and received his Ph.D. from Jawaharlal Nehru University. He obtained his post-doctoral neuroscience research training at Columbia University in
title: How to use your brain's prediction engine to work smarter | Ashok Hegde | TEDxGeorgiaCollege

Foi coordenador do grupo de estudos Relações Internacionais e Mudança Climática na UFPEL. Senior Fellow no Instituto Sul Americano de Política e Estratégia (ISAPE). author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this talk, Behaviour Change specialist, Jemma Joel, explores how small daily choices, paired with honest self-reflection and consistent action, can rewire our habits and transform our lives. Through personal stories and research, it shows that while self-reflection can be uncomfortable, embracing it helps us build resilience, confidence, and lasting change.

 With over a decade of experience in the field of mental health and behaviour change, Jemma has supported thousands of individuals in transforming their mindset, habits, and overall well-being. 

Her work blends evidence-based nutrition and psychology to guide people toward sustainable lifestyle changes rooted in self-awareness and self-compassion. She is especially passionate about helping individuals find balance in their health journey by aligning habits with personal values, rather than restrictive rules. 

Jemma’s approach is holistic and inclusive, with a deep understanding of the emotional and behavioural complexities su
title: Rewiring your life-The power of choice, consistency, and reflection | Jemma Joel | TEDxSwansea Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When technology often feels overwhelming, this talk repositions it as a supportive tool that returns women's most valuable asset—time—while increasing autonomy, control, and options. Using individual experiences and practical illustrations, it conveys a straightforward yet impactful idea: when used purposefully, technology can enable us not merely to keep pace, but to genuinely flourish.

 Dara Kalvort, Corporate VP of Digital Sales & Strategy at Spanish Broadcasting System, drives digital revenue growth across streaming and third-party platforms—and created the game-changing Digidea division. With over 20 years in media sales and a leading voice in AI strategy, she also founded Seize the Day with AI, empowering teams to work smarter, build relationships, and drive impact. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Empowered by Tech, Freed by Choice. | Dara Kalvort | TEDxSwansea Women

description:
Christine LaVopa’s talk shares her journey of breaking the mold, releasing expectations, rebuilding with strength, and stepping into true freedom. Her story invites others to find resilience, healing, and the courage to rewrite the life they deserve.

 Christine  helps high-performing professionals and organizations align success with sustainability. 
With a background as both an athlete and educator, she brings over two decades of experience guiding people at every level, from athletes and executives to children, military, fire, and police personnel.
Her journey, marked by both personal challenges and professional milestones, has shaped her belief that resilience is built through intentional choices. Known for blending science, strategy, and lived experience, Christine equips people with practical tools to lead with greater energy, clarity, and presence.
As a military spouse and mother, she has rebuilt her career and community across multiple moves and deployments, embodying adaptabi
title: Break Your Mold: Freedom to Rebuild the Life You Deserve | Christine Lavopa | TEDxSwansea Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: You know his photographs and his innovations, even if you don't know Harold Edgerton's name.  Milk drops, speeding bullets, hummingbird wings, and high speed machinery, all too fast for the human eye to see, were made visible by Edgerton's stroboscopes and high-speed flash equipment.  Today Edgerton's photos are in the collections of art museums around the world, a fascinating mix of art and science.  In this talk, MIT Museum curator Debbie Douglas, reintroduces Edgerton and shares some of the insights from a new exhibition at the MIT Museum that will open in January 2026. Deborah Douglas has been interested in aerospace history for forty years. Her passion is sharing stories about the history of technology. Amazingly, Douglas’ first job was at the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum, and she has done stints at the NASA Langley Research Center, and Science History Institute before joining the MIT Museum in 1999 as the inaugural curator of science and technology.  She writes bo
title: Freezing TIme: Rediscovering "Doc" Edgerton | Deborah Douglas | TEDxMIT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
When we imagine spaceflight, we often focus on rockets, spacewalks, and distant destinations. But sending humans into space is not just an engineering challenge—it is a biological, medical, and social one.

Drawing on personal experience as a physician and astronaut, this talk explores what happens to the human body and mind in space, from bone loss and cardiovascular changes to stress, isolation, and cultural dynamics aboard spacecraft. It examines how space medicine, telemedicine, and human-centered technologies make long-term spaceflight possible—and how these innovations are already transforming healthcare on Earth. Bernard A. Harris, Jr is a physician, former NASA astronaut, and venture capitalist who has spent more than two decades investing in telemedicine and frontier technologies that connect health, humanity, and innovation. A veteran of space shuttle missions and a key member of NASA’s Commercial Space Committee, he helped shape the strategy that ignited today’s boom in pri
title: What It Takes to Put Humans in Space | Bernard Harris, Jr. | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
India’s journey to the Moon did not begin with powerful rockets or unlimited resources—it began with constraints, creativity, and determination.

This talk traces the evolution of India’s space program, from early, low-capacity launch vehicles to historic planetary missions such as Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan. It explores how frugal engineering, iterative learning, and international collaboration enabled India to achieve the world’s first soft landing near the Moon’s south pole. Beyond the missions themselves, the talk highlights the scientific discoveries, technological innovations, and societal impact of space exploration—from inspiring a new generation to transforming India’s STEM ecosystem. Sreedhara Somanath is an aerospace engineer and the Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), where he has played a central role in shaping India’s modern space program.

Over a career spanning more than three decades at ISRO, Somanath has led the development of multiple launch
title: Building a Spacefaring Nation, One Mission at a Time | Sreedhara Somanath | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The world’s toughest problems are already being worked on—often by people in disconnected networks who rarely get visibility, resources, or support.

In this conversation, Jacqueline Jones and Megan Smith explore how inclusion, technology, and community-driven frameworks can unlock collective genius at a global scale. Drawing on experiences from government, industry, and grassroots innovation, they share practical methods for “scouting” solutions already in motion and “scaling” them by connecting people, data, and institutions. From mapping unmapped cities to empowering local makers, entrepreneurs, and educators worldwide, the talk shows how progress accelerates when we widen the aperture and let more voices lead.

Rather than inventing solutions from the top down, this approach focuses on empowering the doers—proving that with the right networks and tools, almost anything can be fixed. Jacqueline Jones is a leader in partnerships, inclusion, and community engagement at LinkedIn, wher
title: Scout and Scale: Unlocking Collective Genius | Jacqueline Jones & Megan Smith | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
From hospital corridors to boardroom decisions, many women are taught — subtly and consistently — to wait. To wait for the right time, the right approval, or the moment when life feels less uncertain.

This talk explores the cost of that waiting.

Through her journey as a daughter, a mother, and an entrepreneur, the speaker reflects on how postponing action delays not only ambition, but impact. She challenges the belief that there is a perfect moment to begin, revealing how purpose is often discovered through action, not readiness.

Rather than presenting waiting as caution, the talk reframes it as a habit — one that keeps women from stepping into their full influence. By choosing intention over permission, the speaker shows how careers shift, families evolve, and future generations are shaped.

This is a call to stop postponing life.
To begin where you are.
And to move forward — even before everything feels safe. Sonam Garg Sharma is the Founder and CEO of Medical Linkers, a global h
title: What happens when women stop waiting | Sonam Garg Sharma | TEDxGreenfield Women

author: TEDx Talks
description: In a world obsessed with speed, certainty, and immediate answers, curiosity is often rushed — or silenced altogether. We are encouraged to know, decide, and conclude quickly, leaving little room to wonder, question, or explore. This talk invites us to slow down and let curiosity breathe. It explores how curiosity thrives not under pressure, but in openness — when we allow ourselves to ask questions without demanding instant clarity. Through reflection and lived insight, the talk shows how curiosity deepens learning, strengthens empathy, and keeps growth alive at every stage of life. Rather than treating curiosity as a childlike trait to outgrow, the talk reframes it as a lifelong practice — one that requires patience, humility, and space. Because curiosity doesn’t disappear when we stop asking questions. It disappears when we stop listening. And sometimes, the most powerful thing we can do is give curiosity the room it needs to breathe. Shruti Kolarkar is a visual designer and creativ
title: Let Curiosity Breathe | Shruti Kolarkar | TEDxGreenfield Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dacă totul este strategie, atunci nimic nu este strategie. Călin Hințea demontează miturile despre planificarea rigidă și explică de ce strategia nu este o știință exactă, ci o artă a alegerii și a concentrării. Într-o epocă în care viteza schimbării este amețitoare, capacitatea de a nu fi „miop” și de a înțelege paradigma prin care privim lumea devine esențială pentru a evita eșecul.

Prezentarea explorează diferența dintre un lider pur operațional și un strateg adevărat, subliniind că succesul real nu vine din rezolvarea a zeci de sarcini mărunte, ci din identificarea acelor câteva puncte critice care pot genera un efect de domino. De la concepte precum „Grand Strategy” și până la lecțiile filosofice ale lui Sun Tzu sau Marcus Aurelius, acest talk ne provoacă să ne schimbăm lentilele prin care privim realitatea. Strategia înseamnă, înainte de toate, capacitatea de a abstractiza inteligent și de a avea curajul să te focusezi doar pe ceea ce contează cu adevărat pentru a produce rezul
title: RE/Framing Society | Călin Hințea | TEDxCluj

description: Nesta palestra, Alice Pataxó compartilha uma reflexão profunda sobre educação, identidade e pertencimento a partir da sabedoria indígena. Para ela, a escola não é um prédio: é a comunidade, a escuta, a memória e a relação com a natureza. Alice nos convida a repensar como aprendemos, quem ensina e quais conhecimentos escolhemos valorizar. Uma fala que conecta saberes ancestrais, espiritualidade, justiça climática e o papel da juventude indígena na construção de um futuro mais justo, sustentável e coletivo. Alice Pataxó é uma jovem liderança indígena do povo Pataxó, comunicadora e ativista climática. Nascida no sul da Bahia, utiliza as redes sociais e a comunicação para defender os direitos dos povos indígenas e a preservação do meio ambiente. Reconhecida no Brasil e no exterior, Alice participa de debates globais sobre justiça climática e leva a voz da juventude indígena para o mundo, unindo saberes ancestrais e tecnologia. Ela já participou de conferências globais, como a COP26, repre
title: A escola somos nós: uma história sobre a sabedoria indígena | Alice Pataxó | TEDxSaoPaulo

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We celebrate brilliance. We admire talent. We chase genius.
But far less attention is given to the quiet force that shapes all of it: guidance.

This talk explores why raw intelligence alone is rarely enough to create meaningful success. Drawing from years of experience guiding young minds, the speaker reflects on how direction, mentorship, and timely intervention often matter more than innate ability.

Through real-world observations, she shows how potential can remain unrealized — not due to lack of talent, but due to lack of support. Guidance, she argues, doesn’t limit creativity; it channels it. It doesn’t replace genius; it helps it endure.

In a world obsessed with individual brilliance, this talk reminds us that growth is rarely a solo journey — and that the right guidance, at the right time, can change the course of a life.

Because genius may spark possibility,
but guidance turns it into progress. Sheetal Gupta is an educator who works closely with children and young learners
title: Why guidance matters more than genius | Sheetal Gupta | TEDxGreenfield Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Fear is often mistaken for discipline. In homes, classrooms, and institutions, compliance is rewarded while questioning is discouraged — all in the name of “discipline.” But fear may control behavior in the moment; it does not build character.

This talk challenges the idea that fear creates discipline. It explores how fear-based systems silence curiosity, suppress confidence, and replace understanding with obedience. Through reflection and observation, the speaker highlights the difference between discipline that is imposed and discipline that is internalized.

Rather than rejecting structure or accountability, the talk reframes discipline as something rooted in trust, clarity, and purpose. True discipline, it argues, teaches responsibility — not anxiety.

Because fear may stop mistakes,
but it also stops growth.

And if we want disciplined individuals,
we must stop confusing fear with learning. A tech-savvy middle school student actively exploring website development, combining curi
title: Obedience Is Not the Same as Discipline | Devansh Dahiya | TEDxGreenfield Youth

description: Nesta palestra, Patrícia Ellen da Silva parte de uma história pessoal para propor uma nova forma de pensar o futuro. A partir dos ensinamentos de sua avó indígena, ela conecta saberes ancestrais à economia contemporânea e à urgência ecológica do nosso tempo. Patrícia mostra como desenvolvimento econômico e cuidado com a natureza não são opostos, mas partes de um mesmo sistema vivo. Uma reflexão sobre escuta, pertencimento e decisões que respeitam os limites do planeta  e apontam caminhos mais justos, regenerativos e sustentáveis para todos. Patrícia Ellen da Silva é empreendedora da economia verde e atua na interseção entre sustentabilidade, inovação e desenvolvimento econômico. É Brazil Partner da Systemiq e cofundadora da Aya Earth Partners. Foi Secretária de Desenvolvimento Econômico, Ciência e Tecnologia do Estado de São Paulo, onde liderou políticas públicas voltadas à inovação, à transição verde e ao crescimento sustentável. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conf
title: Lições da minha avó indígena sobre economia e ecologia | Patrícia Ellen da Silva | TEDxSaoPaulo

author: TEDx Talks
description: Em um tempo marcado por excesso de informação, polarização e automatismos, Aline Midlej propõe uma reflexão essencial: o que acontece quando deixamos de sentir? Nesta palestra, ela fala sobre o papel da sensibilidade, da empatia e da escuta no jornalismo e na vida. Sentir, aqui, não é fragilidade: é compromisso ético, é presença, é responsabilidade com o outro e com a realidade que escolhemos narrar. Aline convida o público a repensar a forma como consumimos notícias, como contamos histórias e como nos relacionamos com o mundo. Porque informar sem sentir pode nos manter vivos, mas não inteiros. The inner discipline that allows fast, safe movement in extreme terrain Anand Mali is a passionate Mountaineer and a national Level sports climbing athelete who thrives on turning grit into altitude. Recepient of the Best Mountaineer  of the  Year Award. In September 2021, Anand Mali served as the expedition leader for the Giripremi team that achieved the first successful Indian ascent of Mt. Manda-1 (6,510 m) via the challenging North Ridge route — the only successful climb of this peak since a Japanese team in 1984.
